sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive on 17 November 2025, succeeding John Pettigrew, who retired from the role on 16 November 2025 after almost 10 years in post, having joined the board as Chief Executive Designate on 1 September 2025.

sentences.quote: National Grid plc (NG.) has revealed a major overhaul of its operating framework, cutting its Group Executive Committee from 13 to 8 members starting 1 September 2026.
sentences.text: In August 2026 the company announced a new operating structure effective 1 September 2026, placing its businesses under single UK and US geographic leaders and cutting the executive committee from 13 members to eight: Cordi O'Hara as President UK, covering electricity distribution and transmission, and Sally Librera as interim President US pending an internal and external search, with Carl Trowell as President of Global Capital and Alice Delahunty as Chief Technology and Innovation Officer.

citations.quote: National Grid has appointed Zoe Yujnovich as its next chief executive, succeeding John Pettigrew after almost 10 years in the post.
citations.title: John Pettigrew replaced by Zoe Yujnovich, former Shell executive

sentences.quote: Yujnovich will join the National Grid Board as chief executive designate on 1 September 2025 and will be appointed chief executive on 17 November 2025.
sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive in November 2025, succeeding John Pettigrewafter a board succession process, joining from Shell where she was integrated gas and upstream director.

In FY2026 the group reported record capital investment of 11.6 billion pounds, asset growth of 10.9% and underlying EPS up 8% at constant currency, with the total dividend up 3.8% in line with its CPIH-linked policy.

Capital allocation has centred on regulated networks,with National Grid Renewables and Grain LNG divested, alongsidea five-year framework to 2030/31 of at least 70 billion pounds, around three-quarters of it supply-chain secured.

thesis_pillars.text: National Grid plans at least 70 billion pounds of capital investment over the five years from 2026/27 to 2030/31, targeting asset growth of around 10% a year. Its financial outlook for that period sets out cumulative capital investment of at least GBP 70 billion and asset growth CAGR of around 10%. Management guides to 8-10% underlying EPS growth across the five-year framework, with 13-15% underlying EPS growth expected in 2026/27 as higher allowed revenue follows the step up from RIIO-T2 to RIIO-T3. Growth is largely contracted and regulated: around two-thirds is already covered by regulatory agreements. The dividend policy aims to grow per-share payouts with UK inflation; the 2025/26 total dividend was 48.49p, up 3.8% in line with UK CPIH. Delivery is already running at record levels, with underlying EPS up 8% at constant currency and investment of GBP 11.6 billion in 2025/26.
